tn_wall_of_useless_conflict.blurb: A sandstone sport wall at Foster Falls, in the South Cumberland area west of Chattanooga, tucked a little past the Music City and 5.9 sections. It holds sixteen bolted lines, and the character is clearly mid-grade to hard: a handful of routes in the 5.9 and 5.10 range, one easier warm-up, and a big cluster of 5.11s with a single 5.12 on top. Several of the lines are four-star favourites. The wall looks mostly toward the southwest, so expect sun through the middle of the day in the busy season, which makes it a comfortable choice in cool weather. The walk in is longer than at the main crags, which tends to thin the crowds.

tn_bachelor_buttress.blurb: The first wall you meet when hiking up into the Dinner Branch area near Graysville, east of Chattanooga. Sixteen bolted sport lines on sandstone, and it leans hard: only one route sits at 5.10, around five are 5.11, nearly all the rest are 5.12, and there is a lone 5.13. It suits climbers who can warm up on 5.11 and want to work harder lines, with steep, jug-hauling climbing on the best of them. The trail in crosses a creek with no bridge, then climbs steeply uphill, so the spot sees few visitors and feels fairly secluded.

tn_sun_wall.blurb: A ledge-top wall in the North Clear Creek section of the Obed and Clear Creek climbing area, roughly a quarter-hour walk from the South Clear Creek entrance. Sixteen routes, mainly trad with five sport lines, and a spread from an easy 5.6 through several 5.9 and 5.10 lines to a few 5.11s and a pair of 5.12s. Routes run fairly short, which makes it a handy spot for a quick session. Being up on a ledge means it can be awkward if you are hauling a heavy pack, but the wall is sunny.

tn_jerry_s_kids_boulder.blurb: A boulder with a bundle of problems in the Jungle Gym part of Stone Fort (Little Rock City), a wooded bouldering area by a golf course in Soddy-Daisy, north of Chattanooga. Sixteen problems here, running from a single easy line through a solid middle of V3 and V4 to a handful of hard ones between V6 and V8, so it works for people at several levels. The namesake problem is among the most climbed in the area. The cluster sits in a gulley with a small stream; bring pads and a spotter, and expect the occasional patch of pebbles in the stone.
